title: Oman will not extend Salalah port concession beyond 2028; APM Terminals (30% of Salalah Port Services) to exit
summary: Oman's Ministry of Transport notified Salalah Port Services Company that the container and general cargo concessions dating from 1998 will not be extended beyond 1 November 2028, calling the decision final and unconditional. APM Terminals holds 30% and provides technical/operational support under management agreements; a $300m upgrade completed in Q1 2025 lifted capacity from 4.5m to 6.5m TEU and the port handled 4.3m TEU in 2025 (+31%). The successor operator has not been named, opening a major Arabian Sea transshipment hub to competition.

title: Hapag-Lloyd to acquire 25% of APM Terminals Maasvlakte II as Rotterdam mega-expansion proceeds
summary: Hapag-Lloyd agreed to buy a 25% stake in APM Terminals Maasvlakte II in Rotterdam, with APM Terminals remaining operator; price undisclosed and subject to regulatory approval. The expansion adds 1,000m of deep-sea quay (to 2,000m total), extra yard, four new rail tracks and automated equipment, taking annual capacity to 5.4m TEU. The deal cements the Gemini Cooperation partners' joint hub strategy in North Europe.

title: APM Terminals-led Sunset Consortium wins 30-year, ~$600m Puerto Caldera concession in Costa Rica
summary: The Sunset Consortium (APM Terminals, Hapag-Lloyd and part of incumbent Sociedad Portuaria de Caldera) was awarded the 30-year concession to modernise and operate Puerto Caldera, Costa Rica's main Pacific port, with investment estimated at $500-600m across container, bulk and general cargo terminals. Container capacity is expected to roughly triple toward 1m TEU and total tonnage to rise from 6m to 11m t. ICTSI, excluded at the technical stage, filed two challenges that the Comptroller General accepted for review in May 2026.

title: APM Terminals pledges $600m to upgrade Apapa container terminal ahead of 2031 concession expiry
summary: At the Africa CEO Forum in Kigali, APM Terminals' Africa-Europe regional president committed $600m to modernise the Apapa terminal in Lagos and related logistics infrastructure, in a meeting with President Tinubu. APM says it has invested over $438m in Apapa since 2006 and handles about half of Nigeria's containerised trade (Apapa, Onne, Kano). Apapa's share of national throughput fell to 16.7% in 2025 versus 40.6% for Lekki; the 25-year concession expires in 2031 and renewal is undecided.

title: APM Terminals Poti orders $7.1m harbour crane after record 636k TEU year on Middle Corridor gateway
summary: APM Terminals Poti is buying a multipurpose mobile harbour crane for $7.1m (delivery end-2026) as part of a modernisation programme; cumulative investment in Poti exceeds $180m. The terminal handled a record 636,466 TEU in 2025 and 277,081 TEU in Jan-May 2026, and the crane lifts container capacity above 650,000 TEU plus ~500,000 t of other cargo. Poti handles ~80% of containerised ocean cargo for Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan and is a key Caucasus/Central Asia gateway.

title: APM Terminals and Hateco break ground on $1.7bn Lien Chieu container port in Da Nang
summary: APM Terminals and Vietnam's Hateco Group held the groundbreaking for the Lien Chieu port in Da Nang under a long-term (reported 50-year) mandate from Da Nang City. Estimated investment exceeds $1.7bn for eight berths with more than 5.7m TEU annual capacity at full build-out, accommodating 18,000 TEU vessels. Phase 1 (berths 1-2) targets go-live in early 2029, adding a central Vietnam deep-water gateway.

title: APM Terminals Suape: Latin America's first fully electrified box terminal to open H2 2026, phase 2 pulled forward to 2027
summary: APM Terminals confirmed its BRL 2.1bn Suape (Pernambuco) terminal is in final construction with operations starting in H2 2026, with all equipment electric. Initial capacity is 400,000 TEU/yr, a 55% increase in Suape's container capacity. The state governor announced in October 2025 that phase 2 is being brought forward seven years from 2034 to 2027 and that APM has requested additional expansion land.

title: APM Terminals takes 37.5% stake in DP World's South Container Terminal at Jeddah Islamic Port
summary: APM Terminals acquired a 37.5% interest in the South Container Terminal at Jeddah Islamic Port, with DP World retaining 62.5% and continuing to operate under its 30-year BOT concession awarded in 2019. Price was not disclosed. Maersk expects the stake to bring additional vessel calls and transshipment volumes to Jeddah as a Red Sea hub, in a rare DP World-Maersk co-ownership.

title: Maersk Terminals FY2025: revenue $5.3bn (+20%), EBITDA $1.8bn; APM Terminals climbs to No.3 globally with 59.3m TEU
summary: A.P. Moller-Maersk's Terminals segment posted FY2025 revenue of $5.3bn (+20%), EBITDA of $1.8bn (+15%), EBIT of $1.7bn (+31%), ROIC of 16.1% and record 88% utilisation. Dynaliners' 2025 ranking shows APM Terminals handled 59.3m TEU (+11% from 53.2m), moving from fourth to third globally, overtaking COSCO Shipping Ports; PSA led with 69.9m TEU and Hutchison Ports slipped to seventh at 47.6m TEU.

title: APM Terminals named interim operator of Balboa as Panama voids Hutchison's concessions
summary: After Panama's Supreme Court ruled in January 2026 that the law underpinning Panama Ports Company's Balboa and Cristobal concessions was unconstitutional, the government said Maersk's APM Terminals would run the terminals on an interim basis pending a new tender; by March 2026 APM Terminals operated Balboa and MSC's TiL operated Cristobal under temporary arrangements. Hutchison warned APM Terminals of legal action and sought international arbitration. The episode gives APM Terminals a foothold at the Pacific entrance of the Canal.

title: APM Terminals signs exclusive barge and inland terminal lease with Barging Marine Solutions to decongest Apapa
summary: APM Terminals Nigeria signed an exclusive lease agreement running to September 2031 with Barging Marine Solutions (BMS) covering two waterfront/inland container terminals and barge services around Apapa, offering an alternative to trucking. BMS operates the services for APM Terminals and the two will jointly develop customer solutions. The move adds landside capacity while APM weighs further Lagos modernisation.

title: APM Terminals and Enna Group officially open Rijeka Gateway, the Adriatic's most advanced container terminal
summary: Rijeka Gateway, a JV between APM Terminals and Croatia's Enna Group, was officially opened on 29 October 2025 after commercial operations began in September 2025. Terminal investment exceeds EUR 380m (EUR 600m including road/rail links); phase 1 offers 400m of quay and 650,000 TEU/yr, rising to 680m and over 1m TEU after expansion. In its first year it handled 370,000+ TEU with 53% rail share, serving as a Gemini hub for Central Europe.

title: APM Terminals commits EUR 156m to upgrade Barcelona terminal for two simultaneous mega-ships
summary: APM Terminals announced a EUR 156m two-phase investment at the Port of Barcelona: reinforcing quay caissons, deepening the berth to 15m, new rails for five new STS cranes (three already delivered, two due mid-2026), onshore power supply civil works and equipment renewal/decarbonisation. Works began in August 2025 with FCC and both phases complete by Q3 2028, strengthening its Western Mediterranean hub.

title: APM Terminals and Nigerian Ports Authority launch $60m green freight electrification project at Onne
summary: APM Terminals Nigeria and the NPA agreed a $60m, APM-funded project to electrify container freight handling at Onne Port (Rivers State), supporting the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy's low-carbon logistics plan. It forms part of a broader $500m APM Terminals programme to improve efficiency and cut congestion at Nigerian ports, including an electronic truck call-up system.

title: APM Terminals Pecém secures licence to 2049 and announces BRL 200m berth expansion to 850k TEU
summary: APM Terminals Pecém (Ceará) announced a BRL 200m (~$36m) investment alongside a licence renewal through 2049, adding a 350m berth to extend the quay from 600m to 800m and lift capacity from 650,000 to 850,000 TEU by 2029. The terminal handled 325,478 TEU in H1 2025 (+38%) and a record 706,524 TEU in full-year 2025 (+27%), and can receive 400m ULCVs.

title: Maersk and Port of NY/NJ agree 33-year lease extension for APM Terminals Elizabeth to 2062
summary: A.P. Moller-Maersk and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey reached agreement to extend the APM Terminals Elizabeth lease from its 2029 expiry to December 2062, subject to a board vote on 27 March 2025. APM Terminals recently committed a further $200m to modernise the terminal, which handles over 25% of the port's container throughput. The deal locks in a long-term US East Coast gateway.
partners: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey

title: APM Terminals Pipavav signs $2bn MoU with Gujarat Maritime Board for port expansion
summary: APM Terminals Pipavav signed an MoU with the Gujarat Maritime Board for a ~$2bn expansion of Pipavav Port covering container and liquid cargo infrastructure and stronger multimodal links to the Dedicated Freight Corridor, contingent on a long-term concession agreement. The plan is part of Maersk's stated intent to invest over $5bn in Indian ports and maritime infrastructure. Current capacity is 1.35m TEU and 4m t dry bulk.

title: APM Terminals completes 2m TEU MedPort Tangier expansion, lifting capacity to 5.2m TEU
summary: APM Terminals delivered the final stage of a three-year, two-million-TEU expansion of MedPort Tangier at Tanger Med on schedule, taking total annual capacity to 5.2m TEU. The terminal, which added 500 staff in 2023-24, is a core Gemini Cooperation hub from February 2025 and features auto-mooring, digital berth planning and shore power. It competes directly with DP World's Mediterranean and West African hubs for transshipment.

title: APM Terminals extends Aqaba Container Terminal concession by 15 years to 2046 with $242m commitment
summary: APM Terminals and Aqaba Development Corporation agreed a 15-year extension of the Aqaba Container Terminal concession to 2046. The package includes about $242m of investment and development plans targeting net zero by 2040, plus $500,000 for Jordanian capacity-building. ACT handled a record ~898,000 TEU in 2023 (+5.4%) and is the Red Sea gateway for Jordan and Iraq transit trade.

title: PSA takes 49% of Lach Huyen Port Investment JSC to develop $945m four-berth Haiphong terminal
summary: PSA Vietnam agreed to invest in Lach Huyen Port Investment Joint Stock Company, acquiring a 49% stake alongside Lach Huyen International Logistics & Industrial Park, to develop and operate berths 9-12 at the Lach Huyen deep-sea complex in Haiphong. The $945m project will add 4.5m TEU of combined capacity in northern Vietnam. The transaction completed in October 2026 (Allen & Gledhill advised PSA).
partners: Lach Huyen International Logistics & Industrial Park JSC

title: Tuas Port passes 25m TEU since 2022 launch; 14 berths operating, 18 targeted by 2027
summary: PSA Singapore announced that Tuas Port, described as the world's largest fully automated container terminal, has handled 25m TEU since operations began in September 2022. Fourteen berths are operational with a target of 18 by 2027, and PSA's Singapore hub handled a record 44.5m TEU in 2025 with connections to 600 ports. The ramp-up underpins PSA's Node-to-Network strategy and its lead over Jebel Ali as the world's top transshipment hub.
partners: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore

title: Port of Gdansk signs 30-year lease with Baltic Hub for 27ha rail and terminal expansion
summary: The Port of Gdansk Authority signed a 30-year lease with PSA's Baltic Hub Container Terminal for a 27-hectare site next to the T2 deepwater terminal following a competitive tender. Baltic Hub will fund a new rail siding able to handle 750m trains, additional container yards and handling equipment, in phases, to shift freight from road to rail. It follows the June 2025 opening of T3 and PSA's stated ambition of a 7m TEU mega-hub in Gdansk.

title: PSA Intermodal Italy and Logtainer form PSA Padova to run Interporto Padova intermodal terminal
summary: Following a concession award in December 2025, PSA Intermodal Italy and Logtainer signed an agreement to manage and develop the intermodal terminal at Interporto Padova through a new majority-PSA company, PSA Padova; Interporto Padova remains a shareholder. The deal extends PSA's hinterland rail network behind its Genoa and Venice terminals in line with its Node-to-Network strategy.

title: PSA to invest $1bn in PSA Genova Pra container hub
summary: The Western Ligurian Sea Port Authority and PSA Italy signed in Singapore an agreement under which PSA International will invest about $1bn to upgrade the PSA Genova Pra terminal, focused on capacity, automation and logistics efficiency, after approval by the Port of Genoa. It is PSA's largest Mediterranean commitment and reinforces Genoa as its gateway to northern Italy and the Alps.

title: Five mega STS cranes arrive at PSA Antwerp's Europa Terminal under Project Emerald renewal
summary: Five ship-to-shore cranes over 50m high, the largest ever ordered for the Port of Antwerp, arrived at PSA Antwerp's Europa Terminal as part of 'Project Emerald', the multi-phase renewal with Port of Antwerp-Bruges that includes a new deep-water quay for the largest container ships. The cranes (52m high, 71.8m reach, 26 rows) enter service from summer 2026. The programme has been reported at about EUR 335m over nine years and three phases.

title: PSA Panama to lift yard capacity 15% in 2026; 1.35m TEU handled in 2025, $300m+ expansion under study
summary: PSA Panama International Terminal (Rodman, Pacific side) plans to raise static yard capacity about 15% by end-2026 through new empty-container yards and reorganised areas. The terminal handled 1.35m TEU in 2025 (-2.1%), has ~2m TEU capacity, and PSA has invested over $700m in Panama with ~$30m/yr recently; a larger expansion could exceed $300m depending on demand and national port planning as Balboa/Cristobal are re-tendered.

title: PSA International handles record 105m TEU in 2025; Singapore hits 44.5m TEU
summary: PSA International reported record group throughput of 105m TEU for 2025 (+5%), with Singapore terminals at a record 44.5m TEU (+8%) and terminals outside Singapore at 60.4m TEU (+2%). PSA remains the world's largest terminal operator and is positioned to be the first to exceed 70m TEU on an equity-adjusted basis (Dynaliners put its 2025 equity volume at 69.9m TEU).

title: Saudi Global Ports (PSA-PIF JV) to invest SAR 3.5bn in Dammam over five years to challenge UAE hubs
summary: SGP CEO Rob Harrison said the PSA-PIF joint venture will invest SAR 3.5bn (~$930m) in Dammam over five years: SAR 2bn in container terminals, SAR 665m upgrading multipurpose terminals and SAR 670m in the Dammam integrated logistics park, explicitly targeting transshipment share from Jebel Ali and Khalifa Port. King Abdulaziz Port handles just under 3.9m TEU; SGP ran at 122% utilisation in 2024 and operates 5-7 daily Dammam-Riyadh rail services.

title: SGP inaugurates SAR 1.5bn Terminal 2 berth expansion at King Abdulaziz Port Dammam, capacity to 3.8m TEU
summary: Saudi Global Ports (PSA-PIF JV) officially inaugurated the SAR 1.5bn expansion of its second container terminal at King Abdulaziz Port Dammam, adding 225m to the 700m quay so two mega-vessels can berth simultaneously and lifting combined T1+T2 capacity from 2.5m to 3.8m TEU. Mawani and ZATCA officials attended; the project strengthens Dammam as the Gulf-side gateway to Riyadh.

title: SGP breaks ground on SAR 1.3bn, 1m sqm Dammam Integrated Logistics Zone adjacent to the port
summary: Saudi Global Ports broke ground on a ~1m sqm integrated logistics zone next to King Abdulaziz Port Dammam with investment of up to SAR 1.3bn (~$350m), offering modular warehousing (300k sqm Grade A within 18 months), cold chain, vehicle storage, re-export and light manufacturing, petrochemicals and e-commerce areas linked to SGP Intermodal rail. It mirrors DP World's Jebel Ali/Jafza port-plus-zone model on Saudi Arabia's east coast.

title: PSA Mumbai (BMCT) phase 2 inaugurated: $1.3bn project doubles capacity to 4.8m TEU, India's largest terminal
summary: Prime Ministers Modi and Wong virtually inaugurated phase 2 of Bharat Mumbai Container Terminals at JNPA, doubling capacity to 4.8m TEU with 2,000m of continuous quay, six DFC-compatible rail tracks and links to 63+ ICDs on 200 ha. The $1.3bn (SGD 1.7bn) project is the largest Singapore FDI in India, runs on renewable power and makes PSA Mumbai India's largest container terminal, competing with DP World's Nhava Sheva terminals.

title: Baltic Hub opens T3 terminal in Gdansk, adding 1.5m TEU to reach 4.5m TEU
summary: PSA's Baltic Hub inaugurated its T3 deep-water terminal in Gdansk on 6 June 2025, adding about 1.5m TEU and raising annual capacity from 3m to 4.5m TEU once fully operational by end-2025. Attended by PSA Group CEO Ong Kim Pong, the opening consolidates Gdansk as the Baltic's leading transshipment and Central/Eastern Europe gateway.

title: PSA BDP acquires majority stake in Mexican forwarder ED Forwarding on nearshoring demand
summary: PSA BDP, PSA International's supply chain arm, acquired a majority stake in Mexico-based logistics provider ED Forwarding, a partner agent in its network for over a decade; terms undisclosed. PSA BDP cited shippers relocating production from Asia to Mexico. It extends PSA's 'Node-to-Network' logistics push into North American nearshoring corridors.

title: PSA weighs sale of its 20% stake in CK Hutchison's ports business alongside BlackRock-TiL deal
summary: Reuters reported PSA International is exploring the sale of its 20% minority stake in Hutchison Port Holdings, bought for $4.4bn in 2006, contingent on CK Hutchison's $22.8bn EV sale of its 80% to the BlackRock/GIP-TiL consortium proceeding. PSA had shelved a ~$4bn sale attempt in 2023. A disposal would free significant capital for PSA's own expansion programme.

title: PSA acquires 85% of Polish intermodal operator Loconi International
summary: PSA International, via PSA Baltics N.V., agreed to acquire an 85% stake in Loconi International S.A., one of Poland's leading intermodal rail operators, from ATC Cargo, subject to approvals. The deal builds rail products behind Baltic Hub Gdansk and extends reach into Central and Eastern Europe under PSA's Node-to-Network strategy.

title: PSA Sines commissions new mega-cranes as $444m Phase III expansion targets 4.2m TEU by 2030
summary: PSA Sines brought new Super Post-Panamax quay cranes into service in February 2024 (capable of handling 24,000+ TEU vessels), raising capacity from 2.3m to 2.7m TEU as part of a Phase III expansion worth over $444m that will double Terminal XXI capacity to about 4.2m TEU by 2030. Sines is Portugal's largest container terminal and an Atlantic transshipment competitor to Tanger Med and Algeciras.

title: Hutchison Ports and MSC/TiL resume talks on 7m TEU Omega terminal in Rotterdam
summary: Hutchison Ports (ECT) and MSC's Terminal Investment Ltd resumed negotiations to build the Omega terminal in Rotterdam's Europahaven/Prinses Amaliahaven, first announced in 2022, with capacity of up to 7m TEU. No agreement has been reached and the Port of Rotterdam Authority wants a decision by end-2026. Separately, ECT Euromax received ten new Chinese-built cranes in 2026.

title: Hutchison Ports Pakistan orders $76m of electric cranes and trucks for Karachi deep-water terminal
summary: Hutchison Ports Pakistan announced a $76m order of two electric remote-controlled quay cranes, 17 electric RTGs, 70 electric trucks and 50 trailers for its Karachi deep-water terminal (SAPT), with deliveries across 2026-27; 20 e-trucks, 10 trailers, a reach stacker and an empty handler were already received. The order advances its electrification agenda while the larger $3bn expansion remains stalled.

title: Hutchison Ports' $3bn Karachi expansion plan stalls on AD Ports concession clause and procurement rules
summary: Hutchison Ports' proposal, raised from $1bn to $3bn after its CEO met PM Shehbaz Sharif in May 2025, to extend SAPT berthing by ~900m, expand KICT onto West Wharf land and build a logistics park with warehousing, CFS, Ro-Ro and bonded areas has stalled. Officials cite the government's KGTL concession with AD Ports Group, which bars new terminals until Karachi reaches 4m containers, and PPRA tender requirements. About $1.8bn was to be invested over 5-7 years; Karachi/Qasim terminals run at up to 80% utilisation.

title: Hutchison Ports to start four new berths at Sokhna in 2026 as Abu Qir terminal drives Egypt volume growth
summary: In its 2025 review, CK Hutchison said new facilities in Egypt, notably the Abu Qir terminal developed with the Egyptian Navy ($730m, 2m TEU design, 38-year concession), contributed to a 3% rise in group throughput, and that four more berths are scheduled to start in 2026 at Ain Sokhna port (1.7m TEU terminal, part of a $700m Sokhna/B100 Alexandria programme with COSCO and CMA CGM). Hutchison's Egypt investment now exceeds $1.5bn, competing with DP World Sokhna on the Red Sea.

title: CK Hutchison ports division 2025: 90.1m TEU (+3%), revenue HK$48.9bn (+8%), 295 berths
summary: CK Hutchison's ports division handled 90.1m TEU in 2025, up 3% from 87.5m, driven by mainland China exports, Yantian transshipment and new Egyptian facilities; revenue rose 8% to HK$48.9bn (~$6.2bn) with EBITDA and EBIT also up 8% and storage income up 17% (Mexico, Europe). New berths in Saudi Arabia offset the return of concessions in Iraq, leaving 295 berths. Dynaliners ranked Hutchison seventh globally at 47.6m equity TEU, down from fifth.

title: BlackRock-TiL consider carving Panama out of $22.8bn Hutchison ports deal; COSCO could take African ports
summary: A year after the March 2025 announcement, the BlackRock/GIP-TiL consortium is considering excluding Balboa and Cristobal from its $22.8bn acquisition of 43 CK Hutchison terminals outside China/Hong Kong after Panama revoked the concessions. The 145-day exclusivity lapsed in July 2025 without signing amid Chinese regulatory opposition; COSCO-led mainland investors joined talks but stalled on seeking control, and a restructuring under discussion would hand certain African ports to COSCO while TiL-BlackRock keep the rest. Outcome directly reshapes DP World's competitive landscape in Africa and Europe.

title: Panama voids Hutchison's Balboa and Cristobal concessions; Hutchison seeks talks and arbitration
summary: Panama's Supreme Court ruled in January 2026 that the law establishing Panama Ports Company's concession (awarded 1997, renewed 25 years in 2021) was unconstitutional, and the state took control of PPC (90% Hutchison, 10% government). Hutchison formally asked to renegotiate 'absolutely everything', warned of a port shutdown, announced international arbitration and threatened legal action against APM Terminals, named interim operator of Balboa (TiL took Cristobal). Hong Kong and Beijing called the ruling politically motivated.

title: Hutchison Ports invests MXN 3.47bn (~$188m) to expand Lazaro Cardenas container terminal
summary: Hutchison Ports' Lazaro Cardenas unit (LCT, 122 ha) will invest about MXN 3.47bn (~$188m) to expand the container terminal and add new facilities, with crane and equipment electrification underway since 2024. The terminal handled ~1.5m TEU in 2024 and the group is separately expanding its automobile terminal capacity by 20%, competing head-on with APM Terminals' 2.2m TEU terminal in the same port.

title: Yantian posts second straight record year; East Port Phase I to add three automated berths and 3m TEU
summary: HPH Trust's 2025 annual report records a second consecutive annual throughput record at Yantian (Shenzhen), with monthly records broken ten times despite ten typhoons, and continued construction of Yantian East Port Phase I: three fully automated berths adding 3m TEU of annual capacity. The electric truck fleet grew from 83 to 256, Kwai Tsing (Hong Kong) ordered six autonomous e-trucks for 2026, and carbon intensity is down 29% versus 2021.
source_name: Hutchison Port Holdings Trust Annual Report 2025

title: Hutchison Ports commits to expedite $1bn modernisation of KICT and SAPT in Karachi
summary: Pakistan's Ministry of Maritime Affairs said Hutchison Ports committed to fast-tracking its $1bn plan to upgrade Karachi International Container Terminal and South Asia Pakistan Terminals with advanced equipment, electrification, automation and road connectivity; a roadmap and joint working group were agreed. Hutchison says it has paid over Rs225bn in government revenues and employs 5,000 in Pakistan. The pledge later grew to $3bn but has faced regulatory hurdles.

title: CK Hutchison agrees $22.8bn sale of 43 ports outside China to BlackRock-GIP and MSC's TiL
summary: CK Hutchison announced an agreement in principle to sell its 80% controlling interest in Hutchison Port Holdings' non-Chinese assets, 199 berths at 43 ports in 23 countries including Balboa and Cristobal in Panama, to a consortium of BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners and MSC-backed Terminal Investment Ltd for an enterprise value of $22.8bn ($14.2bn equity for the 80%). Hong Kong and mainland China ports were excluded. The transaction, which would make MSC/TiL the world's largest terminal operator, followed US political pressure over the Canal and triggered a Chinese antitrust review.

title: Hutchison Ports hands back Iraq concessions; offset by new Saudi berths, group holds 295 berths
summary: CK Hutchison's 2025 results commentary noted that new berths in Saudi Arabia offset the return of its concessions in Iraq, leaving the ports division at 295 berths worldwide. The exit removes Hutchison from the Iraqi market where DP World and ICTSI are active, while its Saudi footprint (Jazan JCPDI port, SPARK dry port/bonded zone JV) continues to build.

title: Egypt awards Hutchison Ports development of 1.7m TEU Ain Sokhna container terminal; operations targeted mid-2025
summary: Egypt's Ministry of Transport awarded Hutchison Ports the rights in January 2024 to develop the Hutchison Container Terminal at Ain Sokhna Port on the Red Sea: 1,600m of berth (1,200m in the initial phase) dredged to 18m, with 1.7m TEU capacity and operations then expected to begin mid-2025. It is part of a $700m programme (with the B100 terminal at Alexandria) that takes Hutchison's Egypt investment above $1.5bn, placing it adjacent to DP World Sokhna.
